har.title: Weekend schedule
har.subtitle: It's not just Saturday's battle. The event starts already on Thursday and ends on Sunday.
har.thu_what: Arrival, camp, registration, first meetings, evening fire
har.fri_what: In-camp game, accompanying programme, children's game, fair, arenas
har.sat_what_post: , roll-call, approval, armies' march-out, in-game clashes
har.sun_what: Packing up, cleaning, departure, helping the organisers
thu.p1: Thursday opens the weekend. The first participants arrive, the camp goes up, registration starts and people begin to settle into their armies and fellowships.
thu.p2: Thursday is ideal for those who want to arrive in calm, pitch a tent, meet others and tune into the weekend without Saturday's rush.
thu.li1: arrival on site, parking according to instructions,
thu.li3: meeting your army, evening fire and camp atmosphere.
fri.h3: Friday 21 Aug — The camp comes alive
fri.p1: Friday is not the main battle. It's a day when the camp turns into a lively place full of preparations, programme, meetings and smaller games. Suitable for newcomers, families with children, companions, photographers.
fri.li2: children's game, fair and stalls, arenas,
sat.p1: Saturday is the main day. There's the morning roll-call, explanation of rules, registration of latecomers, weapon and costume checks, the calling-out of armies and the main game / battle.
sat.li2: lives assigned according to the costume,
sat.li5: the closing climax of the game.
sun.h3: Sunday 23 Aug — Packing up and departure
sun.p1: On Sunday the camp is packed up, the area cleaned and participants head home. Help with cleaning is welcome and goes a long way to leaving only flattened grass behind.
sun.li1: packing the tent, cleaning the camp,
har.alert_post: If you can, come for the whole weekend — it's easier to join your army, meet people, prepare your gear and experience an atmosphere that doesn't fit into Saturday's battle alone.
eq.title: What to bring
eq.alert_warn_body: On arrival every participant goes through a mandatory safety check of weapon and costume. Without approval you can't play.
eq.alert_info_body: Participants under 18 must bring a written consent of their legal guardians. A form template is in the Registration section.
food.title: Food & drink
food.p1: We as organisers don't provide catering directly. Each participant is responsible for their own food and drink.
food.p2_pre: To make the stay more comfortable, we arrange the on-site presence of the
food.p2_post: pub, where you'll be able to buy food and drink according to its menu and operational possibilities.
food.p3: We recommend bringing your own basic reserve of food and drink, especially if:
food.li4: you expect a heavier physical exertion,
food.li5: you know that without a second supper you turn into an orc.
food.note: There will be drinking water on site in a tank. Don't expect showers, electricity or the comfort of an inn in Rivendell — we're on a meadow, in nature.
kids.title: Children's game
kids.p_pre: For younger participants we are preparing a separate children's game. It runs separately from the main battle and is adapted to the age, safety and abilities of children. The main game is
stalls.title: Stalls and the fair
stalls.p: On site you'll find thematic gear — costumes, fabrics, leather accessories, jewellery, weapons. The organisers do not guarantee the availability of a particular product; if you need something specific, agree with the seller in advance.
